The Hawkeyes will play the Buckeyes at 2:30 p.m. CT on Saturday at Kinnick Stadium in Iowa City. The game will be available on CBS. Iowa has four players listed on Wednesday's injury report, with two of them being listed as out — most notably starting strong safety Tyler Brown. Brown appeared to pull up with a hamstring injury during Iowa's 20-19 win at Michigan, then stayed in the game and surrendered a 48-yard touchdown pass on the next play. Brown continued to play the rest of the fourth quarter and even met with the media on Tuesday this week, but was cagey about his status for the Ohio State game. With Brown sidelined, his likely replacement is Villanova transfer Anthony Hawkins, who started Iowa's first two games of the season. Hawkins won the job after Brown missed all of fall camp with a soft-tissue injury, believed to be a hamstring. Also available to fill in at safety would be Purdue transfer Ty Hudkins and Robert Morris transfer Xavier Styles. The Hawkeyes' starting free safety is Zach Lutmer, who led Iowa with a career-high 12 tackles vs. Michigan. Another report will be released at 7 p.m. CT Thursday as part of the Big Ten's new protocol, with another report at 7 p.m. CT Friday and a final report two hours before kickoff on game day. away.blurb: News Sports Business Opinion Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals FOOTBALL Ohio State football nickel back Jay Timmons questionable for game at Iowa Joey Kaufman Columbus Dispatch Sept. 30, 2026, 8:23 p.m. ET Jay Timmons was listed as questionable on Ohio State’s initial availability report submitted to the Big Ten for its game at Iowa on Oct. 3. Timmons, a freshman who has been the Buckeyes’ starting nickel back this season, left with an unspecified injury during the second half of last week’s win over Illinois . He emerged in September as one of the key pieces for the Buckeyes’ retooled defense, making nine tackles and breaking up four passes. Timmons also forced and recovered a fumble on the first play from scrimmage at Texas. If Timmons is unable to return against the Hawkeyes, coach Ryan Day mentioned as cornerbacks Jermaine Mathews Jr. and Jordan Thomas as other options to take over for him in the slot. The statuses of starting right tackle Phillip Daniels and tight end Bennett Christian are also uncertain this week. They were both listed as questionable. Daniels has been sidelined since the loss at Texas , prompting the Buckeyes to reconfigure the right side of the offensive line. Austin Siereveld has started the last two games at right tackle with Gabe VanSickle at right guard. Christian was out last week against Illinois. The conference’s availability report does not specify the nature of the injuries. The Buckeyes could see the return of starting defensive end Zion Grady, who was left off the report after missing the last two games. The Seminoles listed 10 players as out on their initial injury report Wednesday night . Defensive lineman Darryll Desir, running back Samuel Singleton Jr., wide receiver Devin Carter, defensive backs Karson Hobbs, Jamari Howard, Zae Thomas, and Antonion Cromartie Jr., and linebackers Blake Nichelson, Izayia Williams, and Daylen Green will be unavailable. Miami won at Wake Forest, but it cost them dearly. And with injuries limiting Heisman contender Malachi Toney and taking punishing running back Mark Fletcher Jr. out of the game, Hurricanes fans are hoping the extra day off means they're back and ready to play their normal snaps today against Central Michigan . Toney was never the same after stretching backward to make a catch in the third quarter of the Sept. 18 game against the Demon Deacons. The Canes' leading receiver, second in the nation with 28 catches for 444 yards and tied for fourth with five touchdowns, was used sparingly after that as Darian Mensah and the offense stagnated. Part of that was the subsequent loss of Fletcher, who left during the fourth quarter with an upper-body injury . The senior is Miami's leading rusher with 230 yards and three TDs on 36 carries. Without them and other key offensive pieces, the Canes had to scrap to hold on for the 33-20 win. Two major players on the offense were lost for the season when running back Marty Brown (knee) and wide receiver Joshua Moore (upper body) were among those injured . Brown was the No. 2 running back with 97 yards and a touchdown through three games. Moore was second behind Toney with 107 receiving yards and two TDs, and he placed fourth with seven catches.
